This application coming on for orders this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER 1.These

are the first applications filed under Section 439(2) of CrPC for cancellation of bail in connection with crime no.662/2019, registered at Police Station-Industrial Area, Ratlam under Section 420, 34 of IPC.
2.Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that learned Trial Court has wrongly released the respondents on anticipatory bail.

In such type of cases where forgery of huge amount is involved,
anticipatory bail should not be granted to the accused persons.
3.Learned counsel for the State/respondent NO. 1 has supported the contentions of learned counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: 5.Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned order.
6.This is a case of Section 420 of IPC,triable by learned JMFC.

whereby the learned Judge has released the applicant on anticipatory bail relying upon the judgement passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of [Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar & another [(2014) 32 crimes 40 SC].

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar & another [(2014) 32 crimes 40 SC]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the impugned order, this Court is of the view that no illegality or infirmity is found in the order passed by learned Sessions Judge.

That apart, the bail order has been passed in the year 2019,
i.e. four years back.
The respondents have also not misused the liberty granted to them.
7.In view of above, petitions regarding cancellation of bail filed under Sections 439(2) of CrPC are hereby dismissed.
(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95259876/
